t.7.11.1: But Sumālī, learning that those night-roamers had obtained their boons, cast off his fear and rose up from Rasātala together with his followers.
t.7.11.2: Mārīca and Prahasta, Virūpākṣa and Mahodara, the ministers of that rākṣasa, rose up, greatly enraged.
t.7.11.3: And Sumālī, surrounded by all those bull-like Rākṣasas, approached Daśagrīva, embraced him, and spoke these words.
t.7.11.4: By good fortune, son, this long-cherished wish of yours has been fulfilled, since you have obtained such a boon from the foremost of the three worlds.
t.7.11.5: O mighty-armed one, that great fear caused by Viṣṇu, on account of which we abandoned Laṅkā and went to Rasātala, has now left us.
t.7.11.6: Crushed by him again and again, we abandoned our own abode, and fleeing together, all of us entered Rasātala.
t.7.11.7: This city of Laṅkā, once inhabited by rākṣasas, is ours, and yet it has been settled by your brother, the wise lord of wealth.
t.7.11.9: And you, dear son, will become the lord of Laṅkā, there is no doubt; and you will indeed be the master of us all, O mighty one.
t.7.11.8: If indeed it were possible here to bring it back, O sinless one, whether by conciliation or by gifts, or by force, O mighty-armed one, then our purpose would be accomplished.
t.7.11.11: To Daśagrīva, who had spoken these words, the night-roaming Prahasta addressed this courteous speech, accompanied by its reasons.
t.7.11.10: Then Daśagrīva said to his maternal grandfather, who had come before him: "The Lord of Wealth is our elder; you ought not to speak in this way."
t.7.11.12: O Daśagrīva, mighty-armed one, you ought not to speak like this. Among heroes there is no brotherly affection; hear these words of mine.
t.7.11.13: Aditi and Diti, two sisters who lived together, so it is said, were the exceedingly beautiful wives of Kaśyapa the Prajāpati.
t.7.11.14: Aditi gave birth to the gods, lords of the three worlds, while Diti bore the Daityas, sons sprung from Kaśyapa himself.
t.7.11.15: O knower of dharma, O hero, formerly this earth, with its forests, oceans and mountains, belonged to the Daityas, it is said; they had become mighty.
t.7.11.16: Having slain them in battle, the mighty Viṣṇu brought this imperishable triple world under the control of the gods.
t.7.11.18: Thus addressed by the evil-minded Prahasta, Daśagrīva reflected for a moment and then said, "Very well."
t.7.11.17: It is not you alone who will commit this transgression; it was practised by the gods before. Act upon these words of mine.
t.7.11.19: But on that very day, the mighty Daśagrīva, filled with that same joy, went to the forest together with those night-rangers.
t.7.11.20: Then the night-roaming Daśagrīva, stationed on Trikūṭa, sent Prahasta, skilled in speech, as his envoy.
t.7.11.21: O Prahasta, go quickly and, at my word, speak these conciliatory words to the lord of wealth, the foremost of the Nairṛtas.
t.7.11.22: O king, this city of Laṅkā belongs to the great-souled Rākṣasas, yet it has been settled by you, gentle one. This is not proper for you, O sinless one.
t.7.11.24: Thus addressed, Prahasta, skilled in speech, then went and reported the whole message of Daśagrīva to the Lord of Wealth.
t.7.11.23: Therefore, O you of matchless valour, if you would peaceably hand this city over, my wish would be fulfilled and dharma too would be upheld.
t.7.11.25: Having heard these words from Prahasta, the god Vaiśravaṇa, skilled in speech, gave Prahasta his reply.
t.7.11.26: Go and tell Daśagrīva: 'The city and the kingdom that are mine, this is yours as well, O mighty-armed one; enjoy it, with every thorn removed.'
t.7.11.27: Lord of the Rākṣasas, may good fortune be yours; I will soon carry out all that you have said. But wait a while, until I inform my father.
t.7.11.28: Having spoken thus, the Lord of Wealth went into the presence of his father; having saluted his elder, he told him what Rāvaṇa desired.
t.7.11.29: Father, this Daśagrīva has sent a messenger to me, saying, 'Let the city of Laṅkā, formerly inhabited by hosts of Rākṣasas, be given up.' Tell me, O you of good vows, what I ought to do in this matter.
t.7.11.30: Thus addressed, the brahmarṣi Viśravas, that bull among sages, spoke these words to Dhanada: “Listen, son, to what I say.”
t.7.11.31: The mighty-armed Daśagrīva spoke thus in my presence, and that most evil-minded one was rebuked by me and admonished in many ways.
t.7.11.32: In anger I told him again and again, “Be gone!” Now hear, my son, my words, which are aimed at your welfare and in accord with dharma.
t.7.11.34: Therefore, O mighty-armed one, go to Kailāsa, the mountain that upholds the earth, and settle there to make it your dwelling; abandon Laṅkā together with your followers.
t.7.11.33: Utterly bewildered by the granting of boons, this most evil-minded one does not know who deserves honour and who does not; and because of my curse he has taken on a dreadful nature.
t.7.11.35: There flows the lovely Mandākinī, foremost among rivers, her waters covered with golden lotuses radiant like the sun.
t.7.11.36: It is not fitting for you, O Dhanada, to be at enmity with that rākṣasa, for you know how supreme a boon he has obtained.
t.7.11.37: Thus addressed, he accepted those words out of reverence for his father and departed, together with his wives and citizens, with his ministers, and with his vehicles and wealth.
t.7.11.38: Prahasta went to Daśagrīva and reported everything: "That city of Laṅkā, thirty yojanas in extent, is empty. Enter it together with us and uphold your own dharma there."
t.7.11.39: Thus addressed by Prahasta, Rāvaṇa the rākṣasa then entered the city of Laṅkā together with his brothers, his army and his followers.
t.7.11.40: Then Daśānana, consecrated as king by the night-rangers, settled the city, and that city became filled to the brim with night-roamers resembling dark rain-clouds.
t.7.11.41: Then the Lord of Wealth, out of reverence for his father's words, founded a city on the mountain spotless as the moon, adorned with splendid, well-decorated mansions, like Amarāvatī of Puraṃdara.
